svg.text: EVERY FASTENER PERMUTATION BEHIND THE PLATE
24 combinations: 6 nut constructions x 3 washer options, and with/without threadlocker for the nuts that do not lock on their own.
plate 4.75 mm (0.187 in) - stud 10.00 mm (0.394 in), fixed by the magnet - plate hole O6.5 mm.
Washer thickness is the MAX of the range McMaster sells it to, never the nominal: a stack that must fit has to survive the thickest one shipped.
"bearing" is the annulus the OUTERMOST part presses on the plate with — the washer if there is one, else the nut's own face. Pressure is at the magnet's 26.2 lb.
Nut and washer part numbers are the BLACK-OXIDE ones where stocked; a number in grey means only plain 18-8 exists.
at least 0.50 mm of thread to spare
THIN nylon-insert locknut, DIN 985 low <<< SPECIFIED
within +/-0.50 mm — three stacked tolerances can swallow this; do not build on it
the stud ends before the nut does
SPECIFIED: THIN nylon-insert locknut, DIN 985 low
Of 24 permutations, 7 fit and 1 of those lock MECHANICALLY. The specified stack: +1.25 mm of thread to spare, 45 mm2 of bearing, locking mechanical.

THICKNESS is what runs out in this stack, not diameter: the stud is 10.0 mm (an ESTIMATE for the MM-C-32 until K&J's drawing is read) against a 4.75 mm plate, so a 1.6 mm washer is the difference between fitting and the tolerance band.
No other mechanical-locking stack fits. M6 part numbers are NOT VERIFIED: this catalogue is DIN nominal heights, not McMaster's tables yet.
None of this is close to a bearing problem: even the smallest annulus here is ~96x under A36/1008 mild steel's 36000 psi yield. The stack is decided by THREAD LENGTH and by locking, not by bearing.
